summary: Polk County fire lookout tower reported complete in a March 1933 newspaper item, with a lookout installed; its later history is not in the sources checked.

events.note: Completion reported in a newspaper item dated 30 March 1933

evidence.supports: tower on the old Frostproof road completed
evidence.quote: With the completion of the fire lookout tower on the old Frostproof road

evidence.supports: item credited to the Avon Park Times
purpose: prevention of woods and grass fires
evidence.quote: the prevention of woods and grass fires in this territory has commenced in earnest
the installation of Glen Luke as lookout man

evidence.supports: Luke took charge Wednesday morning and was on duty all day
evidence.quote: Luke took charge of the tower Wednesday morning and is on duty all day.

evidence.supports: tower connected to the fire station by phone
evidence.quote: The tower is connected with the fire station by phone and all evidence of woods or grass fires will be reported immediately.

evidence.supports: fire chief asked anyone intending to burn trash or brush to notify him beforehand
evidence.quote: Fire Chief McCarthy requests that anyone who intends to burn trash or brush notify him

evidence.supports: purpose: avoid unnecessary and expensive runs
evidence.quote: so that unnecessary and expensive runs may be avoided

evidence.supports: lattice observation tower on the map
site at 50 m (164 ft) above sea level

notes_for_editor: The build date and the lookout's installation rest on one reprinted newspaper item, dated 30 March 1933 on the source page and credited to the Avon Park Times (the page also carries '(The Florida Times-Union)'). The item names a fire chief and the fire station but no owning agency, so ownership is unknown. Nothing in the sources checked says what happened to the tower after 1933. The OSM node's edit note reads 'Add/modify AT&T LongLines site' (a MapRoulette task label), so the map entry may describe a different structure at this spot; check before trusting the lattice tag for today. A search snippet from a 2015 Lakeland Ledger article says the Frostproof tower is among three Polk County towers barely standing; that page returned HTTP 403 to our reader, so it is not cited and a human should check it. Not listed on the NHLR or FFLOS Florida lists (checked 2026-10-21). Record elevation_m 50 matches OSM ele. Research used three searches, one over the per-tower cap.
